builder_plan.scenario: Long customer conversations exhaust memory or limit concurrent requests.
builder_plan.change: Change only the attention cache policy, after checking model and runtime support.
builder_plan.baseline: The same model with its ordinary attention cache.
steps: Locate the paper's implementation and check its license, model support, data needs, and hardware requirements. Stop here if you cannot obtain the required artifacts.
Save a small set of representative product tasks and expected outcomes. Keep evaluation tasks out of any training or tuning, and choose quality and cost limits before running.
Run the baseline and the proposed change on identical inputs. Keep other settings fixed and repeat paired runs to expose variation.
Save per-task outputs, failures, timings, and all usage costs. Review regressions before expanding the test.
builder_plan.measure: Peak cache memory, long-context answer quality, first-token latency, and requests completed.
builder_plan.decision: Keep the change only if it meets your preselected quality and latency limits and improves the metric you care about after setup and operating costs. Otherwise retain the baseline. This is an exploration plan, not a validated recommendation.

title: Kernel-based Interpolatory Methods for Context Compression of Attention Mechanisms
summary: The method replaces heuristic token-selection or eviction KV-cache compression with selection of interpolation nodes in the attention kernel's Hilbert space, using GEIM/Q-DEIM with linear-time surrogates (Taylor series, Performer, Random Fourier Features) and streaming updates. Exact node selection costs O(n²) in context length, so practical use requires the surrogate approximations, which add implementation complexity and approximation error; only preliminary LongBench-E results are reported, with performance described as comparable to state of the art rather than superior. Adoption can fail because the surrogate approximations may not preserve the interpolation quality at long contexts, the method is validated mainly on synthetic residual convergence plus preliminary benchmark results, and no mature open-source implementation or production latency measurements are established.
rationale: The approach is mathematically principled and targets a real production bottleneck, but evidence is preliminary (no quantified gain factor, preliminary LongBench-E results only), so small-scale validation against existing KV-cache baselines on the reader's actual workload is warranted before adoption.
